description: A stream read INSIDE a transaction reflects that transaction's own NOT-YET-COMMITTED DML to the stream's base table - the deferred-apply equivalent of read-your-writes. A stored procedure relies on this when it inserts into a table and then reads a stream over that table in the same transaction: without it the stream reads empty and the downstream load silently loads nothing. A ROLLBACK, which just discards the write set, leaves the stream unchanged. Pinned for an APPEND_ONLY stream, for one read after a flush (only the new rows), for rollback, for a standard stream where an UPDATE nets to a DELETE plus INSERT pair, and for a stream over a UNION ALL VIEW where each branch's rows route correctly. The last three are the cross-schema half: change tracking only searched the MUTATED table's own schema for streams, so a stream living in a DIFFERENT schema from its table never saw a committed change at all and rows visible mid-transaction disappeared again at COMMIT - while the widened search must stay EXACT, so two schemas holding a same-named table must not cross-capture. Converted 1:1 from stream/StreamInTransactionTest (now retired); its six same-transaction tests carried an Assumptions.assumeFalse(isLiveSnowflake()) recording a DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED model divergence - frostlake lets a stream read see its own transaction's uncommitted DML, while Snowflake pins a stream read to the transaction's start time and returns nothing for changes made inside it - which becomes skip snowflake with that reason kept.
